title: Applications of ICT
part: Part C — Software and ICT in Life

blocks.html: After studying this chapter you will be able to:

items.html: explain what ICT means
describe how ICT is used in education, health, banking, agriculture, governance, transport, business and entertainment
name important Digital India services and what they do
describe emerging technologies such as AI, IoT and cloud computing

blocks.html: ICT (Information and Communication Technology) is the use of computers, software, networks, the internet and mobile phones to create, store, process, share and communicate information.
ICT = Information Technology (computers and software) + Communication Technology (phones, networks, internet).
Twenty years ago, paying an electricity bill meant standing in a queue at an office. Today the same bill is paid in a minute from a phone. That change is ICT at work.

blocks.caption: Figure 8.1 · ICT in eight sectors of life

items.html: E-learning platforms — DIKSHA (textbooks and video lessons linked to QR codes printed in NCERT and state books), SWAYAM (free online courses) and NPTEL (engineering courses by IITs).
Smart classes — projectors, interactive boards and digital content in classrooms.
Online examinations and results — admission forms, admit cards, results and mark sheets on board websites.
Digital libraries — the National Digital Library of India gives free access to books and papers.
Video lectures and doubt-solving on phones, so a student in a village can learn from teachers anywhere.
School management software for attendance, fees and report cards.
Telemedicine — consulting a doctor through a video call. The government's eSanjeevani service connects patients in rural areas with doctors.
Digital health records — the ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account) number links a person's health records so any hospital can see them with permission.
Hospital management — online appointment booking, billing and pharmacy stock.
Diagnostic machines — CT scan, MRI, ultrasound and ECG machines are computer- controlled.
Robotic and computer-assisted surgery for very precise operations.
Health apps and wearables — step counters and heart-rate monitors.
Core banking — all branches share one central database, so you can use your account from any branch.
ATMs — withdraw cash, check balance and deposit money at any hour.
Net banking and mobile banking — transfer money, pay bills and open fixed deposits online.
UPI (Unified Payments Interface) — launched in 2016 by NPCI; instant payments by scanning a QR code or using a mobile number.
Debit and credit cards, including India's RuPay cards.
Aadhaar-enabled payment — withdraw money at a local banking agent with a fingerprint.
Online trading in shares and mutual funds.
Weather forecasts and alerts by SMS and apps help farmers decide when to sow, spray or harvest.
e-NAM (National Agriculture Market) — an online platform linking mandis so farmers can get better prices.
Soil Health Card — gives test results and fertiliser advice for each farm.
PM-KISAN — income support sent directly to farmers' bank accounts (Direct Benefit Transfer).
Kisan Call Centres and farming apps answer farmers' questions in local languages.
Drones and sensors for spraying, crop health checks and smart irrigation.

blocks.html: E-governance means using ICT to deliver government services to citizens quickly and transparently. The Digital India programme was launched in 2015 to make this possible.

rows: 12-digit unique identity number linked to biometrics
One app for hundreds of central and state services
View land records online (e.g. Bihar Bhumi portal)
Scholarships, pensions and subsidies sent directly to bank accounts

blocks.html: Benefits: less paperwork, less corruption, services available 24 × 7, and time and travel saved.

items.html: IRCTC — online railway tickets; NTES gives live train running status.
FASTag — automatic toll payment using RFID, so vehicles do not stop at toll plazas.
GPS navigation — maps with live traffic.
Ride-hailing apps — book autos, cabs and bikes.
Online flight and bus booking, and digital boarding passes.
Traffic signals and CCTV controlled by computers in smart cities.
E-commerce — buying and selling online.
B2C (Business to Consumer): an online store selling to you.
B2B (Business to Business): a factory buying raw material online.
C2C (Consumer to Consumer): selling your old cycle on a classifieds app.
GST portal — businesses file tax returns online.
Digital marketing — advertising on search engines and social media.
Inventory and billing software in shops; barcode-based checkout.
Video meetings and work-from-home tools.

lessons.title: 8.9 ICT in entertainment, media and science

items.html: Entertainment — OTT video platforms, music streaming, online and mobile games, e- books.
Media — digital newspapers, news apps, podcasts and social media.
Science and space — ISRO uses supercomputers to design and track satellites and missions.
Weather and disasters — IMD uses satellites and computer models to forecast cyclones and heavy rain, and alerts are sent to phones.
Defence — radar, secure communication and simulation for training.

rows: Computers that learn from data and make decisions
Voice assistants, translation into Indian languages, chatbots
Everyday objects connected to the internet
Smart meters, smart bulbs, soil- moisture sensors
Using storage and software over the internet

blocks.html: Did you know? India's UPI handles more real-time digital payments than any other system in the world, and several other countries have adopted it.
Aim: To explore how ICT is used in daily life and in government services.

items.html: Family ICT survey. Ask five family members or neighbours which digital services they use (UPI, IRCTC, DigiLocker, online classes, telemedicine). Record answers in a table.
Offline vs online. Pick one task, such as paying an electricity bill or booking a train ticket. Write the steps for doing it offline and online, and compare time, cost and effort.
Explore UMANG or DigiLocker. With your teacher, open the website and list ten services offered. (Do not enter personal details on a school computer.)
Scan a DIKSHA QR code. Scan the QR code printed in any of your textbooks with a phone and note what content opens.
Emerging tech hunt. Find three examples of AI or IoT in your locality, such as a smart meter or a voice assistant.

blocks.html: Record: Make a chart: Sector – ICT service – Benefit with at least ten rows.

items.html: ICT combines information technology and communication technology.
Education: DIKSHA, SWAYAM, smart classes, online results.
Health: telemedicine (eSanjeevani), ABHA health records, computerised diagnostics.
Banking: core banking, ATMs, net banking, UPI, cards, Aadhaar-enabled payments.
Agriculture: weather alerts, e-NAM, Soil Health Card, PM-KISAN, drones.
E-governance under Digital India: Aadhaar, DigiLocker, UMANG, DBT, online land records.
Transport, business, entertainment and science all depend on ICT.
Emerging technologies: AI, IoT, cloud, robotics, 3D printing, AR/VR, blockchain.
